METHOD (for the note)
- Frames the task as a POMDP, with ReAct-style trajectories (rationale before each action).
- Task knowledge: the agent first trains on expert trajectories to become an "experienced agent". It then re-explores the training tasks to produce rejected trajectories. The agent model itself compares chosen and rejected trajectories to write task knowledge (workflow, commonsense), as in Eq 4. Even when the rewards are equal, the sampled trajectory counts as rejected, because expert trajectories are shorter.
- State knowledge: summarized per step from expert trajectories and stored as (previous action, state knowledge, next action) triplets in a kNN base.
- Two LoRAs on one backbone: the agent model (conditioned on task knowledge) and the WKM (generates task knowledge, then state knowledge).
- Inference: the WKM writes task knowledge once and appends it to the prompt. At each step it generates state knowledge, retrieves N triplets whose previous action matches, and builds p_know from the counts of the next actions. This is mixed with the agent's first-token action probabilities: argmax of γ·p_agent + (1-γ)·p_know (Eq 13). State knowledge is never in the agent's context.
- Datasets: ALFWorld, WebShop, ScienceWorld. Train sizes 3,119 / 1,824 / 1,483. Test: ALFWorld seen 140, unseen 134; WebShop 200 (no unseen split); ScienceWorld seen 194, unseen 211.
- Expert trajectories come from ETO [44]: human-annotated for ALFWorld; GPT-4 filtered to reward >0.7 for WebShop; heuristic golden paths for ScienceWorld. GPT-4 added the rationales.

LIMITS
- Authors concede: (1) it is hard to know what a language model knows or does not know; (2) text-only world knowledge, no multimodal; (3) the WKM cannot update dynamically with world changes or agent feedback; (4) extra inference overhead (about 2.5x).
- It is not a true world model: it cannot be combined with search such as MCTS to predict the world. The authors leave this for future work.
- The ethics statement says a maliciously modified WKM could steer the agent to unethical behavior.
- Not shown: only simulated text environments; only 7-8B backbones trained, with GPT used only for task-knowledge guidance in the weak-guide-strong test; no confidence intervals or multiple seeds reported. Gains over ETO/KnowAgent are 1-5 points.
- State knowledge depends on a training-set knowledge base, so its benefit shrinks on unseen tasks.
- The "unified WKM is key to AGI" remark is speculation.
- Dated: baselines are 2023-early 2024 (GPT-4-0613, Mistral-7B-v0.2, Llama-3-8B). Prompt-only ReAct numbers on these models are not representative of current models.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
ReAct [54] Yao et al.; Reflexion [40] Shinn et al. 2023; NAT [49] (negative-aware training); ETO [44] Song et al. 2024 (Trial and error, DPO-based); KnowAgent [64] Zhu et al. 2024; AutoGuide [6] Fu et al. 2024 (prompts partly taken from it); DPO [36] Rafailov et al. 2023; LoRA [12] Hu et al. 2022; LlamaFactory [62]. World-model line: Hao et al. 2023 (RAP, [10]); Hu & Shu 2023 (LAW, [13]); Ha & Schmidhuber 2018 [9]; Huang et al. 2022 (LMs as zero-shot planners, [14]). Datasets: ALFWorld [41] Shridhar 2021; WebShop [53]; ScienceWorld [50]. Mental models: Johnson-Laird 1983 [18] and 2010 [17]. Agent tuning: FireAct [2], Agent-FLAN [3], AutoAct [34].

CODE: none in the paper. The prompts in App I (Figs 11-13) are images and not in the text layer. The training-format example is in Figs 7-8, p.18-19. The core decision rule is Eq 13: a_{t+1} = argmax_i [γ·p_agent(α_i) + (1-γ)·p_know(α_i)]

- Fig 2, p.3: the full pipeline: (a) task knowledge synthesis, (b) state knowledge summarization, (c) training, (d) planning with the mixing formula. It is the best single diagram for the note.
- Fig 3, p.7: ablation bars on Mistral-7B across ALFWorld, WebShop and ScienceWorld.
- Fig 4: human dataset-level vs. instance-level knowledge.
- Fig 5: single-task vs. multi-task WKM.
- Fig 6: explicit state knowledge.
- Fig 9, App F: win rate of planning steps.
- Fig 10, App H: ETO vs. WKM case study on "clean some soapbar and put it in cabinet". ETO shows "Blind trial-and-error" and "Hallucinatory action" (it puts the soapbar in the cabinet after closing it). WKM goes straight to toilet/sinkbasin.
